title: Rev. Thomas Barnes et al. v. Presbytery of Evangel
disposition_detail: The Assembly approved the Judicial Commission’s report not sustaining the complaint. Before ordaining Mercer, Presbytery was required to have a written call in hand and was responsible for issuing it. The report also requested referral of the general question defining a valid call to the Permanent Committee on Judicial Business.
first_summary: The Judicial Commission did not sustain a challenge to Presbytery’s approval of Mercer for ordination as an evangelist without an existing call and for parachurch work outside its bounds. It nevertheless required a written call before ordination and requested referral of the general question of a valid ministerial call to the Permanent Committee on Judicial Business. No reason was given for rejecting the complaint.
summary: The Fifth General Assembly approved its Judicial Commission’s refusal to sustain a complaint challenging Presbytery’s approval of Mercer for ordination as an evangelist without a call and for parachurch work outside its bounds. No reason for rejecting the complaint was stated. The ruling nevertheless required Presbytery to have—and itself issue—a written call before implementing the ordination decision, and requested referral of the broader question defining a valid ministerial call to the Permanent Committee on Judicial Business.

sources.supports: Complaint, asserted constitutional grounds, referral to the Commission, Assembly adoption, disposition, qualification concerning a written call, and requested committee referral.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: The complaint and parties appear at lines 9–25; the Assembly approved and admitted the Commission report at lines 53–59 (printed p. 89).
evidence_notes.dispute: The challenge concerned approval for ordination without a call, for parachurch work outside Presbytery’s bounds, and alleged conflicts with BCO provisions; lines 11–41 (printed p. 60).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The complaint was not sustained, but a written call was required before ordination and the general call question was requested for referral; lines 85–89 (printed p. 89). No rationale for non-sustenance is stated.
evidence_notes.qualifications: Non-sustenance did not authorize immediate ordination: Presbytery first had to issue and possess a written call; lines 87–89.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No other judicial decision was incorporated by reference; the Assembly adopted the Commission’s own report, lines 53–59.

source_limits: The record gives no reason for refusing to sustain the complaint and does not include the Permanent Committee’s response to the referred question.

score_reasons.concrete_dispute: Identifies the challenged ordination approval, absent call, parachurch work, and geographic issue.
score_reasons.decision: States non-sustenance, the preordination requirement, and the requested referral.
score_reasons.decisive_reason: Faithfully reports that no reason was stated.
score_reasons.distinctive_value: Preserves the important distinction between rejecting the complaint and requiring a written call before ordination.
score_reasons.fidelity: Distinguishes allegations, the Commission’s ruling, and the Assembly’s adoption.
score_reasons.economy: Retains only facts needed to understand the dispute, result, and qualification.

verification_notes: Rechecked lines 53–59 and 85–89; the final summary clarifies that the Assembly approved the Commission’s ruling, that Presbytery itself was responsible for issuing the written call, and that the referral concerned the broader call question rather than the complaint itself.
